questions.question: Explain how occupational segregation contributes to gender wage gaps. / Examine the challenges in achieving gender equality and suggest
questions.solution_html:
• Occupational segregation—where men and women are concentrated in different jobs or
  • industries—significantly contributes to the gender wage gap by channeling women into
  • lower-paying sectors and undervalued roles. Occupational segregation- horizontal
  • vertical-Femaledominated occupations (e.g., nursing, teaching, and administrative work)
  • tend to pay less than maledominated ones requiring comparable skills and education
  • gender pay gap widened in 2025, with women earning 78 cents for every dollar earned by
  • men in the U.S. -Occupational segregation remains one of the leading contributors to this
  • reversal of progress, alongside workforce participation trends and caregivingrelated
  • career breaks- Lower-Paid Sectors Are Female-Dominated- Limited Access to High
  • Paying Roles- Barriers to Promotion.[Give (5 marks) for any five points with explanation]
questions.final_answer: Paying Roles- Barriers to Promotion.[Give for any five points with explanation]
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how occupational segregation contributes to gender wage gaps. / Examine the challenges in achieving gender equality and suggest
questions.solution_html:
• Occupational segregation—where men and women are concentrated in different jobs or
  • industries—significantly contributes to the gender wage gap by channeling women into
  • lower-paying sectors and undervalued roles. Occupational segregation- horizontal
  • vertical-Femaledominated occupations (e.g., nursing, teaching, and administrative work)
  • tend to pay less than maledominated ones requiring comparable skills and education
  • gender pay gap widened in 2025, with women earning 78 cents for every dollar earned by
  • men in the U.S. -Occupational segregation remains one of the leading contributors to this
  • reversal of progress, alongside workforce participation trends and caregivingrelated
  • career breaks- Lower-Paid Sectors Are Female-Dominated- Limited Access to High
  • Paying Roles- Barriers to Promotion.[Give (5 marks) for any five points with explanation]
questions.final_answer: Paying Roles- Barriers to Promotion.[Give for any five points with explanation]
